images.title: One kilogram, four packets
images.purpose: Set up the question: 1 kg of rice is packed into 4 packets of equal weight; how heavy is each packet?
images.composition: One tall upright bar on the left, and a column of four equal packets on the right, each packet level with one part of the bar.
images.exact_structure: Left: one tall vertical bar for 1 kg, split by 3 grey #6B7280 lines into 4 exactly equal stacked parts, all plain. Right: 4 rice packets of exactly the same size stacked in a column, filled teal #0072B2, each one level with one part of the bar. The top packet outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7 with a question label. No fraction written anywhere. Exactly 1 bar, 4 equal parts, 4 packets.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any fraction or weight for one packet written in the frame, or packets of different sizes
images.takeaway: Share the 1 kg equally among the 4 packets.
images.description: A tall 1 kg bar in 4 equal parts beside a column of 4 same-size rice packets, the top packet marked ? kg.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to match each packet with one part of the bar and say what share of 1 kg one part is.

image_decisions.why: Matching each packet to one equal part of a 1 kg bar is the method cue, and it keeps the answer hidden.
